PullRequest.Title: sessions: open existing cloud automation runs without the extension provider
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to #349155. When the Copilot Chat extension does not contribute its cloud session provider, the Agents window can open an existing `copilot-cloud-agent:/task/<id>` automation run through core's account-bound GitHub Tasks client. Opening reads the task and its paginated conversation. A text reply sends one `/steer` request to that same task and observes its response. No task is created, no automation is redispatched, and no sandbox connection is needed.

The extension remains the default owner when present, even if it is still activating. An explicit `github.copilot.chat.cloudAgent.enabled: false` is not a request for fallback. The core path is for automation tasks only; it does not migrate ordinary cloud sessions, schedules, definitions, or the execution backend. This first adapter renders text conversation history, not the extension's PR or tool cards.

**Validation:** `pnpm run build-fast --client-only` passed. `node_modules/.bin/tsc --project ./src/tsconfig.json --noEmit --skipLibCheck --pretty false` and `pnpm run valid-layers-check` passed. Targeted oxlint and formatting passed. The following Chromium selection passed (440 tests):

```sh
node test/unit/browser/index.js --browser chromium --reporter dot \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/providers/copilotChatSessions/test/browser/cloudAutomationTaskConversations.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/providers/copilotChatSessions/test/browser/githubCloudAutomationStore.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/copilotChatSessions/test/browser/copilotChatSessionsProvider.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/copilotChatSessions/test/browser/cloudAutomationStore.test.ts
```

**Manual check still pending:** In a signed-in window with cloud automations enabled and the extension's cloud contribution absent, reopen an older run from Automations. Verify the transcript appears without creating a run; send a text reply to a designated test task and confirm it appears on the original GitHub task. Repeat with the extension present to check the original route, and with the cloud-agent setting explicitly off to check that core does not take over. No live task was modified during local validation.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The two callers, five-second rescheduling, serial pagination, page size, transport revalidation, and desktop IPC path are directly traced. This is static evidence; typical transcript size, server latency, and ETag availability determine magnitude.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Sequential GitHub task/event HTTP requests, desktop IPC response bodies, and repeated JSON parsing and event allocations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N events, each read performs one task GET plus P event-page GETs, normally P = ceil(N/100), capped at 100 pages. Both polling loops repeat this traversal after a five-second delay; ID deduplication happens only after fetching. Different task IDs do not coalesce.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive recurring network/IPC traffic and transcript-size-dependent latency before newly generated output can be observed
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Without the extension provider, core did not load or poll task transcripts. Existing automation-history refreshes read run summaries and active task details, not every event page. The extension-owned route is unchanged.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new read() always starts event pagination at page 1. Both the active-history scheduler and followReply() invoke it repeatedly, even when only a new tail event—or no event at all—has appeared.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added lines 195–197 create a fresh Map and restart the full page traversal for every read(); added line 239 calls read() from the rescheduled history observer, and line 294 calls it inside the reply-following loop.
Findings.Title: Avoid rereading the entire transcript on every poll
Findings.Impact: Opening a long-running automation with hundreds or thousands of tool/session events, or replying to an older run, repeatedly revisits all historical pages. This consumes GitHub request capacity and delays showing fresh output behind the old-page round trips, even when most events are not rendered by this text-only adapter.
Findings.Evidence: read() awaits each getEvents() sequentially until the complete event total is collected. The observer reschedules five seconds after completion while the task is active and has a history listener; RemoteChatSessionRestorer subscribes to that event. followReply() likewise scans the complete history before sleeping five seconds. TasksClient.getEvents() requests one page when maxPages is omitted. Transport ETags can reduce transferred HTTP bytes but still revalidate each page, return the cached body across desktop IPC, and parse it again; in-flight sharing does not eliminate successive polls. Thus a 1,000-event run requires 11 sequential HTTP operations per iteration, not one incremental check. The downstream restorer can suppress unchanged model mutations, but not these requests or allocations.
Findings.Recommendation: Separate initial full loading from ongoing observation. Use the existing page API and retained snapshot for a page-aware refresh that reconciles mutable pending events and falls back to full reconciliation on discontinuities, rather than replaying every historical page on each poll.

Scenarios.Scenario: Window registration, automation listing without opening a conversation, extension ownership, and explicit cloud-agent opt-out
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Registration waits reactively for installed-extension registration before enabling fallback. Listing the new controller returns only previously resolved items; its refresh is empty. With an extension declaring the cloud session type, resolution continues through the existing extension command. Explicit opt-out declines fallback.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Installed extension contributions and locally opened task IDs; no transcript-size-dependent work before a conversation is requested.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One fallback registration per default provider; observable lifetime stores dispose registrations when ownership, configuration, or account access changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Extension ownership is observed from extension-change events, and fallback access is derived from existing account-bound store state. Observing taskAccess does not acquire an API client or start task discovery. Existing automation catalogue/history initialization predates this diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced registration, controller refresh/items, provider routing, and the already-existing CloudAutomationStore initialization.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The installed extension count affects a small contribution scan; no evidence establishes a meaningful performance problem there.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable eager startup or listing regression. The newly registered controller starts no filesystem, subprocess, database, IPC, or network work merely by being registered or listed. Extension implementation details remain external to this fallback.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve and open a completed automation run, including warm reopening and task-only hydration for local archive actions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An unresolved resource first waits for provider activation and one task GET to publish its item. Opening content then waits for another task GET and every event page before turnHistory and remote-model restoration can proceed. Task-only resource resolution does not load event pages.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET the exact task and sequentially GET its paginated event history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally 2 task GETs plus P event GETs for a previously unresolved cold open; 1 plus P if resource resolution is already satisfied. Task-only hydration needs one task GET.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Without the extension there was no core conversation reader; native resolution delegated to the extension command. The new one-time transcript read is required to provide the added functionality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All event pages complete before content is returned; the cold task resolution completes before the session can be opened.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire the shared-process account client and send each task/event API request, returning its response body to the renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One retained client lease per store lifetime, shared with existing automation operations; normally one request IPC per logical HTTP operation. Concurrent identical GETs may share transport work but still have caller-side response handling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The infrastructure and account lease cache already existed; this diff introduces task-conversation requests through it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Desktop content loading awaits each request/response. Browser clients execute locally instead of using this request IPC.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse task/event JSON, validate events, deduplicate page overlaps, and construct text history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Linear in returned event payload bytes and event count per full load; overlapping event IDs are deduplicated after retrieval.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No fallback transcript parsing occurred. The existing remote restorer and its cooperative scheduling are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes before initial content and model restoration. RemoteChatSessionRestorer subsequently applies model mutations cooperatively.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One exact task ID and N task events; normally P = max(1, ceil(N/100)) event pages, with a 100-page cap. No automatic discovery across all automation runs is introduced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Initial task and event pages are serial. Different resources can resolve concurrently, bounded by the shared request queue: defaults are 12 global/host, 10 account, and 8 caller-active requests. No subprocess or database boundary is reached by the new reader.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: GitHubCloudAutomationStore.withClient shares and retains the account-client acquisition promise. ChatSessionsService joins concurrent content resolutions by resource and returns cached sessions on a warm hit. HTTP ETags can save body transfer but revalidate over HTTP. Closing/disposal can require a later fresh content load; no negative transcript cache is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced UI openRunSession(), provider resolution, content-session coalescing/cache, typed Tasks client, native IPC, transport ETag behavior, and restorer.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold-open latency depends on page count, event payload size, network round-trip time, and whether a client lease is already available; no measured timings are available.
Scenarios.Verdict: The one-time complete read is intentional functionality, not independently reported. Its reuse by recurrent polling, rather than cold loading itself, creates the reported issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Observe an opened queued or in-progress automation until it becomes terminal
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial content uses the cold-load path. Once RemoteChatSessionRestorer subscribes to history, each scheduled refresh awaits task details and the complete event history before publishing an update. These reads are off the initial opening path but gate fresh transcript updates.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/providers/copilotChatSessions/browser/cloudAutomationTaskConversations.ts: read() lines 189–213 and refresh scheduler lines 236–257
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Revalidate/read the task and every event page from page 1 on every refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: 1 + P serial GETs per successful iteration, including when history has not changed. For 1,000 events this is 11 GETs per iteration. Event-page failures may terminate a partial traversal; retryable failures back off.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing automation listing polled summaries and active task details, but no core fallback loop repeatedly read complete event transcripts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: New history is unavailable until all historical pages finish. Polls use the default interactive lane because only caller is specified.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward each desktop poll request to the shared process and return response text.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally 1 + P request IPC exchanges per iteration. ETag revalidation still returns a cached response body to the caller.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No core task-transcript polling IPC existed on this scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each exchange is awaited within the serial transcript traversal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reparse and allocate a complete event snapshot, rebuild markdown history, and compare it with prior restored turns.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Full returned payload/event processing per refresh even with HTTP 304s. The restorer skips identical model mutations, so unchanged history is not claimed to rebuild the DOM.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing restorer supported history updates, but this adapter newly feeds it complete periodic reconstructions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Parsing and history construction precede publication; downstream equality avoids some model work but cannot avoid the already-issued requests.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P historical event pages per active observed task, repeated five seconds after each completed refresh. Multiple task IDs have independent observation loops; repeated IDs within pages do not reduce request count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Normally one serial polling chain per content session, self-rescheduled only after completion. Different task IDs remain independent, subject to the shared 8-per-caller/10-per-account/12-global limits. Terminal tasks stop rescheduling; disposal cancels the observation token.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The API client lease remains warm. There is no snapshot/page reuse in read(); each call creates a new Map. HTTP validators reduce response bytes when available, not sequential revalidation count. In-flight GET sharing does not coalesce successive iterations. The observed emitter's last-listener hook cancels the scheduled timer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the polling call graph, page restart, fixed delay, listener subscription, transport cache behavior, and shared limiter are directly established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical event counts, time spent actively observing tasks, ETag availability, and request latency are unmeasured; these affect severity, not the existence of repeated boundary work.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one medium-severity repeated-work regression: complete historical pagination repeats on every poll and delays detection of fresh output. No unsupported claim of an unbounded concurrent request burst or full DOM rebuild is made.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send a text follow-up to an existing automation and observe the reply
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The handler first reads a complete baseline, then cancels passive observation, issues exactly one steer mutation, and repeatedly rereads task details and every event page to identify the confirmed echo and stream new answer events. Both sending the steer and observing its output are gated by full scans.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the complete baseline; POST one user_message to /tasks/{id}/steer; repeatedly GET the task and its entire paginated event history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One non-replayed steer per handler invocation, with full baseline and repeated 1 + P_i GET traversals. followReply() waits five seconds after each traversal, not between individual pages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Core had no absent-extension reply adapter. Extension-owned replies remain on their previous route; no task creation or automation redispatch is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The baseline scan delays the actual send. Each later scan must finish before new reply output is delivered.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward baseline reads, the single steer, and observation reads through desktop request IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request exchange per logical API operation, plus cancellation signaling for an outstanding canceled passive read. The account-client lease is reused.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These fallback reply requests did not exist before the diff; the transport infrastructure itself is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited for baseline completion, steer acknowledgement, and each reply snapshot.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize one reply body; repeatedly parse and scan all historical events, then reconstruct final text history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Reply-body serialization occurs once per steer. Event processing is linear in full snapshot size on every observation, despite the seen-ID Set suppressing duplicate emitted answer parts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No core fallback reply serialization or observation existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Old-event parsing/scanning precedes delivery of newly discovered answer parts.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One target task, its P pre-existing event pages, and K reply-observation iterations. Roughly (1 + P) baseline reads, one mutation, and a further 1 + P_i reads per iteration as history grows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The baseline can briefly overlap the passive observer; identical transport reads can coalesce. Passive observation is canceled before steering. Reply polling is serial and all API calls remain globally bounded by the shared queue. The handler itself adds no separate global limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm session and API-client caches avoid reconstructing the session/client, but the handler deliberately rereads baseline and event pages. seen suppresses duplicate progress output, not requests. ETags do not remove per-page round trips or renderer parsing. An uncertain steer is propagated rather than replayed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: directly traced the baseline await, cancellation order, one steer call, repeated read() loop, output deduplication, and transport path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Reply duration, old transcript size, and service latency determine total repeated work; no benchmark or live task interaction was performed.
Scenarios.Verdict: The same full-history polling root cause is covered by the submitted finding rather than duplicated. Single-steer semantics, cancellation, and absence of redispatch do not establish another performance issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Close a content model or invalidate fallback ownership through account/client, extension, or configuration changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Disposal cancels linked session/request tokens and scheduled refreshes. Registration lifetime disposal removes contributions/controllers and disposes cached contributed content. The old account grant refuses further work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cancel an already-outstanding desktop request when the combined token is invalidated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cancellation signal per outstanding remote operation; none per historical event. Later calls through expired access are rejected before issuance.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The shared cancellation infrastructure already existed; the new adapter links its requests to session and account lifetimes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Stops obsolete work; no synchronous cleanup subprocess, filesystem traversal, or database operation is added.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Currently loaded content sessions and at most their outstanding operations; retained opened items are lightweight task-list records rather than complete transcripts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cleanup cancels existing operations rather than launching replacement transcript loads. Newly established accounts may run the pre-existing automation-store refresh, which is not introduced by this change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Account/client reset cancels the grant lifetime and clears the cached client lease/promise. Provider disposal removes cached contributed sessions; RemoteChatSessionRestorer disposal calls session.dispose(). Transcript snapshots and event-ID Sets belong to those content lifetimes. Opened item records remain intentionally available in the controller listing until controller disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced scope cleanup, account lifetime invalidation, contribution removal, ChatSessionsService disposal, and restorer ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of concurrently loaded sessions varies, but no unbounded heavyweight retained resource without cleanup was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No independent cleanup-lifecycle or unbounded-retention regression established. Timers, linked cancellation listeners, and content-session scopes have traced disposal owners.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all 10 changed files and all diff pages against base 0d15d4d60248e35fac1a3fe234d74ed780e15691. Submitted one medium-severity finding for full-transcript pagination repeated by both observation loops. Account/client caching, HTTP ETags, content-resolution coalescing, shared request limits, renderer equality suppression, and cancellation/disposal were accounted for. No concrete old performance-regression fix with qualifying provenance was identified. Review is static; no live service timings or repository execution were used.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
